title: The Artefact
intro: At the gate, a digital artefact wakes up. Pages of Japan are missing. The family is asked to recover them — not from a screen, but from the real world.
history: Airports are modern temples of departure. Nothing sacred happens here except leaving.
mythology: The first kami in this chronicle is not Japanese. It is curiosity.
food: Whatever Japan has already smuggled into the terminal.
weird: Japan is already in this building if you look.

title: The Stacked City
intro: Tokyo did not spread. It stacked. Under the neon is a wet-land village that learned to go vertical.
history: Edo became Tokyo in 1868. The swamp was filled, then layered with rails, basements and towers.
mythology: Cats that beckon. Foxes that wait in Kyoto. Here the spirits wear shop signs.
weird: A tower whose height is a pun.

title: The Ledger of Hope
theme: Spirits, emperors, and names on wood
intro: Kyoto kept the old capital’s manners. The mountain of gates is not a royal project. It is thousands of private prayers.
history: Emperors sat here for a thousand years. Ordinary people paid for the orange tunnel.
mythology: Inari’s messengers are foxes. They carry keys, jewels and rice.
weird: A shrine that is also an account book.

title: The Kitchen
intro: Osaka sold things when Kyoto prayed and Edo ruled. The missions here will arrive with the trains.
history: Merchant city. Kuidaore: eat until you drop.
food: Takoyaki, okonomiyaki, everything on a stick.
weird: A city that brags by feeding you.

title: Memory
theme: What happened, who it happened to, what came after
intro: The artefact goes quiet. This chapter is not scored like the others. It is a record.
history: 6 August 1945. A city of people. Then the bomb. Then the decision to remember in public.
food: Okonomiyaki, rebuilt like the city: layers.

title: The Floating Gate
intro: An island where the gate stands in the sea. Missions follow.
history: Itsukushima. No births or deaths on the sacred island, once.
weird: Deer who know tourists carry biscuits.

title: The Remaining Castle Town
intro: A city the bombs missed. The old districts are not a reconstruction.
history: Maeda domain. Gold leaf, gardens, a temple full of tricks.
mythology: Ninja as theatre and as engineering.
food: Gold on ice cream, if you let it.
weird: A temple designed to confuse an army.

title: Mountain Morning
intro: The Alps hold older houses and stranger winters.
history: Sake towns, merchant streets, thatched villages nearby.
mythology: Mountain kami who do not care about trains.
weird: Houses built to shed snow like a hat.

title: The Old Road
intro: A walk between post towns. The chronicle wants blisters, not Wi-Fi.
history: Nakasendo: the inland road between Edo and Kyoto.
food: Gohei mochi, grilled on a stick.
weird: A town that hid its wires so the road still looks like 1800.

title: Clay and Fire
theme: One of the Six Ancient Kilns
intro: A pottery town next to the airport. Earth, fire, teapots.
history: A thousand years of kilns. Red clay that does not leak.
mythology: The fox of Inari also guards rice bowls.
weird: A giant teapot as a landmark.

title: The Recovered Chronicle
intro: Last dinners. Last pages. The artefact asks what you will keep.
history: Ebisu is named after a luck god who also sells beer.
mythology: The chronicle closes, not the country.
weird: A luck god in a shopping district.
